name: Tressette
description: Tressette is one of the great Italian card games. It is a partnership trick-taking game for 4 players using a 40-card Italian deck. The unique ranking (3-2-A high) and the lack of trumps create a pure suit-following game where communication and memory are paramount. There are 11 points per deal.

history.origins: Tressette originated in Italy and is first recorded from the early 18th century; its lack of trumps suggests it may be older. It is one of Italy's major national card games alongside Scopa and Briscola. The name may derive from "Tre Sett" (three sevens): Cäsar (1800) states that a player holding three sevens could declare and win. The game spread to former Italian-influenced regions including Albania, Montenegro, coastal Slovenia and Croatia, and the Canton of Ticino; the Austrian game Trischettn in South Tyrol is a derivative.
timeline: Early 18th century: first recorded in Italy (Naples).
history.cultural: One of the two 'national' Italian card games alongside Briscola.

rules.objective: Score more points than opponents. Game to 21 (or 31/41).
rules.gameplay: 1. Deal 10. 2. Accuso (optional declarations: Napoletana = 3-2-A of same suit = 3pts; 3 or 4 of same honor = pts). 3. Play 10 tricks: Must follow suit. No trumps. Highest of led suit wins. 4. Score: A=1, 3/2/K/Kt/J= 1/3. Last trick=1. Total 11/hand.

strategy.basic: Lead your long suits. Save Aces for capturing. Win the last trick (1 pt bonus).
strategy.intermediate: Signal to partner through legal means (the order of played cards can convey information).
strategy.advanced: Count all 40 cards. Calculate exact remaining holdings. Control which suit is led.
tips: The last trick is always worth fighting for.
